assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
assertions.evidence: Options are in three separate columns: 'Fragile', 'Insured Value', 'Handling' — not collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500].

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method present. Options are manually constructed in test method: 'options.setFragile(fragile); options.setInsuredValue(insuredValue);' etc.

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Dimensions column shows '[20, 15, 10]', '[30, 20, 15]', '[70, 50, 10]' etc. as single list values in one column.

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: Two @TableTest methods: 'shouldCalculateShippingCost' (14 rows covering rates/surcharges) and separate 'carrierDoesNotAffectShippingCost' (carrier equivalence).

assertions.text: Parameter types correspond to the ShippingCostCalculator.calculateShippingCost interface — weight, cost, and dimension types match the method signature.
assertions.evidence: Parameters: 'double weight', 'List<Integer> dimensions', 'BigDecimal cost' match expected interface types.

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names describe conditions: 'EU standard light', 'EU express medium', 'Dimensional weight override', 'Fragile surcharge', 'Oversize surcharge'.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
assertions.evidence: Columns use mixed naming: 'Region', 'Speed', 'Weight', 'Fragile', 'Insured Value', 'Handling' instead of 'Zone'/'Options' as single columns; missing domain grouping.

assertions.text: Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 2 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: Output contains no TestNG syntax: no @DataProvider, @Test(dataProvider=...), Object[][], or TestNG imports (org.testng.*).
The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit:1.2.1 as a test dependency
The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
The generated tests pass when executed against ShippingCostCalculator
The build file no longer declares a TestNG dependency — the old framework is fully removed, not just the test code.
assertions.evidence: Build file has no TestNG reference
